display_name: DOJ/FTC Antitrust Guidelines for the Licensing of Intellectual Property (2017): the safety zone, the modes of analysis and the particular restraints, as what the agencies say they will do. Agency enforcement policy, not law.
seat: a party to an intellectual property licensing arrangement (the licensor or a licensee), asking what the agencies say they will do with it
scope: AGENCY ENFORCEMENT POLICY, NOT LAW: results say what the Department of Justice and the Federal Trade Commission say they will, may or would be likely to do, never what is lawful. Encoded: coverage (1.0, n.1, n.8); reach (2.1); market power never presumed from protection (2.2, 5.3); the concerns (3.1); whether a technology market (3.2.2, n.33) or research and development market (3.2.3) is analysed; the equal-share rules (3.2.2 via Example 2, 'will assign'; 3.2.3, 'may assign'); Example 3's four-entity screen; horizontal and vertical relationships (3.3, n.27); per se or rule of reason and the depth of the inquiry (3.4, 5.1, 5.5); exclusivity in effect and the two statements that a license 'generally' raises no concern (4.1.2); what the agencies do on their findings (4.2); the 4.3 safety zone in full (facially anticompetitive, twenty percent of each relevant market significantly affected with exactly twenty inside, the goods-markets-only rule, the four-or-more criteria for technology and research and development markets without usable share data, n.58, n.86); price maintenance (5.2); tying (5.3); exclusive dealing (5.4); pool exclusion, future-technology terms and settlements (5.5); grantbacks (5.6); merger analysis of transfers (5.7, n.85); enforcement of invalid rights (6). Reported, never weighed: the considerations of 4.1.1, 4.2, 5.4 and 5.6. Inputs, never computed: market definition and shares, market power, close substitutes, efficiency-enhancing integration, reasonable necessity and every other finding the guidelines leave to the agencies. Answers NOTHING where the text states no outcome, for impossible shares, for contradictory findings, and for a trademark license.

forks.F1: 'collectively account for' is the sum of each party's own share
forks.F2: each relevant market considered must meet its criterion; the failing markets are named
forks.F4: 'facially anticompetitive' is decided by the type of restraint (or always or almost always harmful), whatever its integration
forks.F5: 3.4's list of per se types is open
forks.F6: with accurate share data, technology and research and development markets are tested at twenty percent
forks.F7: a goods market without usable share data has no criterion: NOTHING
forks.F8: a license that only in substance transfers rights (n.85): the zone answers NOTHING; Example 10 is read as an exclusive license in fact under 5.7 (the Example's own reason, the acquisition of a potential competitor, is not computed)
forks.F9: 'absent extraordinary circumstances' is kept in the result's name, not taken as an input
forks.F12: 5.6's offsetting effects are considered only once a significant reduction in incentives is determined
forks.F13: Example 3's screen and 4.3's research and development criterion use the same count
forks.F14: a trademark license: NOTHING (not covered, n.1)
forks.F15: when goods-market analysis is inadequate, goods markets are still considered
forks.F17: 4.1.2's 'only if' states nothing on its other side; exclusive dealing is a restraint on the licensee
forks.F18: Example 2's equal-share sentence is a general rule for technology markets
forks.F19: the safety zone's gates in the order coverage, n.58, merger analysis, condition (1), condition (2)
forks.F20: section 6: one input for both sentences' 'other elements'; fraud without them states nothing under the fraud sentence, and inequitable conduct is not a section 2 basis unless there are both fraud and the elements
forks.F21: 3.1 with no concern, and Example 3 with fewer than four and no significant risk: NOTHING

not_reviewed.note: No domain expert has read this against the guidelines, and no independent test pass has been made. The fixtures for Examples 4, 5 and 9 are not independent of the 3.2.2 competitor test. See NOTES.md sections 1 and 9.
